title: Grateful Dead Live at Swing Auditorium on 1969-12-13
lineage: 7" Master Soundboard Reels > Cassette > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Clear sound‑board recording with solid audio quality highlights a fiery Lovelight and strong mid‑set jams despite a short, slightly uneven show.
ai_review.review: The GD69‑12‑13 soundboard tape is generally clear and well‑balanced, though a few listeners note occasional static and the missing tail of Black Peter. Musically the night shines on Lovelight (Jerry’s scorching guitar, Pigpen’s legendary rap) and the China Cat > I Know You Rider jam, with high marks for Black Peter, Cumberland Blues, High Time and Good Lovin'. The set is brief (≈11 songs) and a bit ragged in places, but most fans find it an enjoyable snapshot of the 1969 era.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈80%) award 4‑5 stars and praise both performance highlights and sound quality; only a few note sloppiness or missing material, so the combined show (70 % weight) and recording (30 % weight) yields a strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced tape for '69 with nice fidelity; occasional static and the final portion of Black Peter is cut, but overall very listenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A short, ~11‑song set that feels a bit incomplete (missing the end of Black Peter) yet maintains strong energy; transitions—especially St. Stephen > Lovelight and the China Cat jam—are praised.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar on Lovelight 'smokes' and his mid‑song solo is highlighted; vocals described as heartfelt.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass lines in the China Cat jam are called 'great' and generally strong throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s rap on Lovelight is celebrated as one of his best, with high energy and memorable vocal moments.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ lick during the Lovelight break is noted; overall keyboards praised for clarity.
